notes:
Overview: Enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity to support customer-facing chat + high-throughput reranking pipelines. Primary ask: predictable throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for multi-region deployments behind VPC.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-02-20: Discovery call (Marissa, Diego, CTO Rajiv Mehta). Collected baseline QPS and latency targets.
- 2026-02-25: Security intake submitted; asked for SOC2 report, KMS integration options, and data residency controls.
- 2026-02-28: Kickoff POC meeting (fireflies: ff_20260228_01_summitforge_kickoff). Agreed on model candidates and sizing approach.
- 2026-03-01: Baseline throughput run against in-cloud hosted endpoint. 95th pctl latency observed ~210ms for 512-token context on llama2-70b-chat-v1 in FP16.
- 2026-03-03: Dedicated test #1: reserved 4xA100-80GB pool, quantized weights (int8/awq prototyping). Throughput improved x2; p95 fell to ~145ms when enabling KV cache for repeated-session traffic.
- 2026-03-04: Onsite infra call w/ SummitForge infra and security. They requested deterministic SLO language for p95 and planned fallback routing to smaller models when capacity constrained.

Use-case specifics / requirements summary:
- Workloads: primary = persistent-chat support agent (low-latency, conversational), secondary = reranking pipeline (high-throughput batched requests).
- Latency targets: target p95 <= 120ms for short chat turns (<=128 tokens), p95 <= 300ms acceptable for long-context generations (>=512 tokens). Absolute SLOs required for SLA.
- Throughput targets: steady-state 180 inference requests/sec for short-turn chat across 3 AZs; batch reranking workload ~4000 sequences/minute (32-token rerank).
- Cost sensitivity: high — wants reserved capacity economics vs burst pricing.
- Model preferences: prefer open models (Llama2-70b-chat candidate) with Redwood-verified quantization profiles. Will accept smaller models for cold-fallback but needs quality regression testing.
- Routing/fallback: policy must support canary/dedicated fallbacks (route to hosted lower-cost model during maintenance).
- Residency: EU data residency required for 30% of traffic; routing by region mandatory.

Model-specific dedicated tuning notes (POC findings):
- Context length: SummitForge needs mixed context usage. Chat sessions average 320 tokens, but escalation cases require 2–6k token contexts. Dedicated pool must allow pinned instances with extended KV cache and memory budgeting for longer sequences.
- Quantization profiles: AWQ-int8 gave best throughput but small quality regressions on sensitive finance prompts (numerical accuracy). We validated int8 + per-layer FP16 for attention layers as a compromise. Need Redwood Optimize runbook to recommend profiles per-model.
- Batching & concurrency: Continuous batching with adaptive max-batch-size worked for reranking (batch=64 optimal on A100-80GB). For chat, smaller micro-batches (~8) with low tail-latency fast-path needed.
- KV cache sharing: Significant win for persistent chat; sharing session KV across pinned GPUs reduced compute 30% and lowered p95 ~40ms. Need discussion on privacy model / retention controls.
- Kernel selection & compilation: Some custom kernels for 70B reduced token-step time by ~12% — require Redwood engineering sign-off for private deployment.

SLA / commercial notes:
- Customer requests committed throughput slots (reserved capacity) with crediting for unused capacity during ramp-downs. They requested explicit p95 and error-rate terms plus rolling maintenance windows.
- Legal asked to cap RTO for model failover and require a fallback model with documented latency envelope.

Open questions / blockers for close:
- Finalized quantization profile trade-offs and acceptance criteria for numerical QA.
- Legal redlines on SLA: customer wants financial credits for missed p95 (negotiation ongoing).
- Exact GPU sizing: SummitForge asking to test a 6x A100-80GB pool vs 8x to balance cost. Need Redwood sizing simulation.

Next steps (owner: Marissa):
- Deliver reserved-GPU sizing proposal with cost scenarios (4x/6x/8x A100-80GB) and expected throughput/latency envelopes (due 2026-03-09).
- Run 7-day throughput soak POC with 6x A100 setup, cross-region enabled, quantization profile int8+fp16 attention. Collect token-level latency heatmaps.
- Prepare SLA term sheet draft and hand to legal for preliminary review.
- Coordinate with Security to finish questionnaire (Nina).

CRM quick notes / quotes:
- CTO Rajiv: "We will not accept unpredictable tails — p95 guarantees are deal-breakers."
- Infra lead: "KV cache saving is huge for us but must adhere to retention rules."
